gaps.detail: The behaviour exists. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/src/routes/$.tsx has a beforeLoad that throws redirect({ to: '/signin' }) for any unknown path. The /signin guard skipWhenSignedIn (/home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/src/lib/guards/skip-when-signed-in.ts) then sends a member with an organization on to /app, and returns early for a visitor. The shell test at apps/web/src/components/shell/shell.test.tsx:172 covers only unknown /app/* paths. docs/spec/auth-onboarding.md:313 and :519 require these legacy-URL cases. Removing or changing the root catch-all would therefore break no test. Render /reading, /ready and /ready/company-1, and assert that a signed-in member with an organization ends on /app and a visitor ends on /signin. Low impact, because the behaviour works today.

gaps.feature: pg-boss start is undone when creating the health queue fails
gaps.detail: Confirmed. /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/jobs/pg-boss.ts:13-14 runs `await boss.start(); await boss.createQueue('health')` with no try/catch. If createQueue throws, pg-boss stays started. The catch in openData (/home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/open-data.ts:77-81) closes only storage and the connection, and it cannot stop a boss it never received. Impact is low, because main.ts calls process.exit(1) on a boot failure. Fix: try { await boss.createQueue('health') } catch (err) { await boss.stop(); throw err }.

gaps.feature: Landing canonical origin from PUBLIC_SITE_URL in apps/landing/.env (canonical, og:url, og:image, robots Sitemap line, sitemap)
gaps.detail: apps/landing/astro.config.mjs line 8 sets `site: process.env.PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? 'https://example.com'`. Astro evaluates the config before it loads .env files, so a value in apps/landing/.env never reaches process.env. The value only takes effect when it is exported in the shell or CI environment. apps/landing/src/lib/config.ts derives SITE_URL from import.meta.env.SITE, which comes from `site`, so siteLink(), robotsTxt() and @astrojs/sitemap all fall back to https://example.com. PUBLIC_APP_URL is read through import.meta.env in config.ts, so it does work from .env. That explains the reported repro, where links used app.test but canonical and robots used example.com. apps/landing/.env.example says these values are 'read at build time', which is misleading. docs/spec/web-shell-landing.md line 384 names PUBLIC_SITE_URL as the source for canonical, og:url, og:image and sitemap. saas-base hardcodes https://example.com in src/index.html (lines 18, 20, 26), src/robots.txt (line 13) and src/sitemap.xml (line 4), and has no env variable. So this is a defect against the arrakit spec and its documented .env setup, not a missing saas-base feature. Fix: in astro.config.mjs, use `loadEnv(process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'production', process.cwd(), '')` from vite, or Astro's envField or schema. Add a test that builds with a .env file. src/lib/config.test.ts only covers the defaults.

gaps.feature: Stale-chunk recovery reloads only on a navigation, and targets the screen being navigated to
gaps.detail: apps/web/src/components/shell/root-layout.tsx useStaleChunkRecovery() listens to every window `vite:preloadError` event. It calls onPreloadError(event, router.latestLocation.href, window) with no check that a navigation is in progress. apps/web/src/router.tsx sets `defaultPreload: 'intent'` with `defaultPreloadStaleTime: 0`. TanStack Start code-splits route components, so hovering or focusing a link runs the route's lazy import. In a production build, Vite's __vitePreload helper (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js about line 27077, handlePreloadError, wrapping `baseModule().catch(...)`) dispatches vite:preloadError when that chunk is stale. onPreloadError in apps/web/src/components/shell/stale-chunk.ts then calls preventDefault and win.location.assign with the current location. A pointer hover can therefore hard-reload the current screen, and anything typed on it is lost. In saas-base, recoverFromStaleChunk runs only from withNavigationErrorHandler in apps/web/src/app/app.config.ts:20-22, with the failed navigation's error.url as the target (shared/stale-chunk.ts:31). apps/web/src/components/shell/root-layout.test.tsx (around line 60) only checks event cancellation and has no case for a preload. Fix: recover only while a navigation is pending, for example when router.state.status === 'pending' or the pending location differs from the resolved one, and use the pending location as the target. Otherwise leave the event alone so a later real navigation reaches RouteError.

gaps.feature: Router load-error screen (RouteError errorComponent): stale-chunk reload of the target route, non-chunk error screen and Try again
gaps.detail: apps/web/src/components/shell/route-error.tsx is wired as the root errorComponent in apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:34. It is the only router-level caller of recoverFromStaleChunk, using router.state.location.href. It reports other errors through reportError and renders the unreachable title and body, with a Try again button that runs reset() and router.invalidate(). No test or e2e spec imports RouteError or makes a route throw. The "Couldn't reach Arrakit." assertions in apps/web/src/components/shell/shell.test.tsx:149, apps/web/src/components/shell/pages.test.tsx:126 and apps/web/e2e/shell-signed-in.spec.ts:81 all reach the /unavailable page (unavailable-page.tsx), not RouteError. stale-chunk.test.ts tests only the pure functions. Removing the errorComponent, changing the target URL or breaking Try again would leave every test green. Suggested RTL test: make a route's beforeLoad or component throw TypeError('Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: https://x/a.js'), then assert that window.location.assign is called once with that route's URL. Then throw a plain Error and assert that the "Couldn't reach Arrakit." heading appears and that Try again re-runs the load.
